definition: Linux architecture consists of hardware, kernel, system libraries, shell, and user applications. The boot process initializes hardware and loads the operating system.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers troubleshoot server startup failures, kernel issues, and system availability problems.
real_world_scenario: A production server does not boot after maintenance. Engineer must understand BIOS, GRUB, kernel loading, and systemd startup.

architecture_flow.diagram: Hardware → BIOS → GRUB → Kernel → systemd → Services

core_concepts.name: Kernel
core_concepts.definition: Core component managing CPU, memory, devices and processes.
core_concepts.usage: Handles communication between hardware and applications.

core_concepts.name: systemd
core_concepts.definition: Linux service manager and init system.

comparisons.summary: Kernel manages hardware while OS includes kernel plus utilities and applications.

definition: Linux filesystem organizes files and directories using a hierarchical structure starting from root (/).
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers need filesystem knowledge for deployments, logs, and troubleshooting.
real_world_scenario: Application logs fill the /var partition causing production outage.

definition: Linux commands are utilities used to interact with files, processes, networking, and system resources through the command line.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers use commands daily for deployment, debugging, automation, and server management.
real_world_scenario: An application is failing in production and an engineer uses grep, find, ps, and logs commands to identify the issue.

architecture_flow.diagram: User → Shell → Linux Command → System Resource

core_concepts.name: find
core_concepts.usage: Used for locating logs and configuration files.

comparisons.summary: find searches live filesystem while locate uses an indexed database.

follow_up_questions: How to find recently modified files?
common_pitfalls: Using inefficient commands on large files

definition: Linux text processing tools allow extraction, transformation, and analysis of text data.
why_it_matters: Production troubleshooting depends heavily on analyzing logs quickly.
real_world_scenario: A server generates millions of log lines and engineers extract only failed requests using awk and grep.
follow_up_questions: Write command to find top IPs from logs

definition: Linux permissions control access to files and directories using read, write, and execute permissions for users, groups, and others.
why_it_matters: Incorrect permissions can expose sensitive data or break applications.
real_world_scenario: A deployment fails because the application user cannot read configuration files due to incorrect ownership.

core_concepts.name: chmod
core_concepts.definition: Command used to modify file permissions.

core_concepts.name: chown
core_concepts.usage: Assign files to users or groups.

comparisons.summary: chmod changes permissions while chown changes ownership.

definition: Linux user and group management controls identities and access privileges.
why_it_matters: Production servers require controlled access and proper privilege management.
real_world_scenario: A new developer requires server access with limited permissions.

core_concepts.name: sudo
core_concepts.definition: Allows users to execute privileged commands.

definition: A Linux process is a running instance of a program managed by the kernel.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers troubleshoot high CPU, memory leaks, and stuck applications.
real_world_scenario: A production application consumes all CPU and must be identified and restarted.

definition: Service management in Linux controls background applications using init systems like systemd.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers manage application availability by starting, stopping, restarting, and monitoring services.
real_world_scenario: A web application is down because the service stopped after a server reboot.

core_concepts.name: systemctl
core_concepts.definition: Command-line tool to manage systemd services.
core_concepts.usage: Start, stop, restart and check service status.

comparisons.summary: systemctl is modern systemd-based management while service is older compatibility interface.

definition: CPU monitoring tracks processor usage, load, and performance bottlenecks.
why_it_matters: High CPU can cause application slowdown and outages.
real_world_scenario: A production API becomes slow because one process consumes 100% CPU.

core_concepts.name: Load Average
core_concepts.definition: Average number of processes waiting for CPU.

definition: Linux memory management controls RAM usage, caching, swapping, and process allocation.
why_it_matters: Memory problems cause crashes and application failures.
real_world_scenario: A server crashes because applications consume all available memory and OOM killer terminates processes.

core_concepts.name: Swap
core_concepts.definition: Disk space used as overflow memory.

core_concepts.name: OOM Killer
core_concepts.definition: Kernel mechanism that kills memory-heavy processes.

definition: Disk management involves monitoring, partitioning, mounting, and managing storage devices in Linux.
why_it_matters: Disk issues are common production incidents that can stop applications and databases.
real_world_scenario: A production server stops accepting requests because the filesystem reaches 100% usage.

architecture_flow.diagram: Disk → Partition → Filesystem → Mount Point → Application

core_concepts.name: LVM
core_concepts.definition: Logical Volume Manager provides flexible storage management.

comparisons.summary: df shows filesystem usage while du shows directory-level usage.

definition: A filesystem defines how data is stored, organized, and retrieved from storage devices.
why_it_matters: Applications depend on correct filesystem configuration and mounting.
real_world_scenario: A database cannot start because its data volume was not mounted after reboot.

comparisons.summary: Partition divides storage while filesystem organizes data.

definition: Linux networking enables communication between systems using protocols, IP addressing, and ports.
why_it_matters: Most DevOps incidents involve connectivity or network issues.
real_world_scenario: An application cannot connect to another service because of a network configuration issue.

comparisons.summary: TCP provides reliability while UDP prioritizes speed.

definition: Advanced Linux networking covers DNS resolution, routing, NAT, packet forwarding, and network security controls.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers troubleshoot application connectivity, cloud networking, and production traffic issues.
real_world_scenario: An application is running but users cannot access it because DNS or routing is misconfigured.

core_concepts.name: DNS
core_concepts.definition: Domain Name System converts hostnames into IP addresses.

core_concepts.name: NAT
core_concepts.definition: Network Address Translation modifies IP addresses.

comparisons.summary: Public IP is internet reachable while private IP is internal network address.

definition: Linux networking commands help diagnose connectivity, ports, DNS, and traffic problems.
why_it_matters: Fast troubleshooting of network issues is a key DevOps skill.
real_world_scenario: A service is running but API requests fail because the port is not reachable.

comparisons.summary: ping tests network reachability while curl tests application endpoints.

definition: Linux firewall controls incoming and outgoing network traffic using security rules.
why_it_matters: Incorrect firewall rules can expose systems or block applications.
real_world_scenario: Application is running but blocked because required port is closed.

definition: SSH is a secure protocol used to remotely access and manage Linux servers.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers frequently manage production servers remotely using SSH.
real_world_scenario: An engineer cannot connect to a production VM and must troubleshoot SSH authentication.

core_concepts.name: sshd
core_concepts.definition: SSH server daemon running on Linux.

comparisons.summary: Passwords rely on secrets while keys use cryptographic authentication.

definition: Package managers install, update, remove, and maintain software packages on Linux systems.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers manage dependencies and application installations.
real_world_scenario: A deployment fails because a required package version is missing.

comparisons.summary: apt is used on Debian systems while yum/dnf is used on RedHat systems.

definition: Linux logging records system and application events used for troubleshooting and auditing.
why_it_matters: Logs are the first source of information during production incidents.
real_world_scenario: A service crashes and engineers analyze logs to identify the failure reason.

definition: Kernel troubleshooting involves diagnosing issues related to Linux kernel, drivers, hardware communication, and system crashes.
why_it_matters: Kernel-level problems can cause server crashes, unexpected reboots, and hardware failures.
real_world_scenario: A production server reboots unexpectedly and engineers investigate kernel logs.

core_concepts.name: dmesg
core_concepts.definition: Command displaying kernel ring buffer messages.

core_concepts.name: Kernel Panic
core_concepts.definition: Critical kernel failure causing system halt.

comparisons.summary: Application crash affects one service while kernel panic can stop the entire system.

definition: Shell scripting automates Linux tasks using command sequences, variables, loops, and conditions.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers automate repetitive operational tasks using scripts.
real_world_scenario: A script automatically checks server health and restarts failed services.

definition: Cron is a Linux scheduler used to execute tasks automatically at defined times.
why_it_matters: Many operational jobs like backups and cleanup run through scheduling.
real_world_scenario: A backup job runs every night using cron.

definition: Environment variables store configuration values used by applications and shells.
why_it_matters: Applications depend on environment variables for configuration and secrets.
real_world_scenario: Application fails because DATABASE_URL variable is missing.

definition: Production troubleshooting is the systematic process of identifying and resolving live system issues.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers are responsible for system reliability and uptime.
real_world_scenario: Application outage occurs and engineer investigates CPU, memory, logs, network, and services.

core_concepts.name: RCA
core_concepts.definition: Root Cause Analysis identifies underlying reason.

definition: Python is a high-level programming language widely used in DevOps for automation, scripting, API integration, and infrastructure management.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers use Python to automate deployments, monitoring, cloud operations, and repetitive tasks.
real_world_scenario: A DevOps engineer creates a Python script to check server health and send alerts automatically.

core_concepts.name: Variable
core_concepts.definition: A name that stores a value.

core_concepts.name: Data Types
core_concepts.definition: Categories of values like string, integer, list, dictionary.

comparisons.summary: Shell is better for simple OS commands while Python handles complex automation logic.

definition: Python collections are built-in data structures used to store and organize multiple values.
why_it_matters: Automation scripts process large amounts of configuration and system data.
real_world_scenario: A deployment script stores server details in dictionaries and processes multiple hosts.

comparisons.summary: List can change while tuple cannot.

definition: Mutable objects can be modified after creation while immutable objects cannot be changed.
why_it_matters: Understanding object behavior prevents unexpected automation bugs.
real_world_scenario: A script modifies configuration data unexpectedly because a mutable object reference was shared.

comparisons.summary: Mutable changes existing object while immutable creates a new object.

definition: Python scope defines where variables can be accessed. LEGB means Local, Enclosing, Global, and Built-in scope.
why_it_matters: Scope understanding prevents variable conflicts and automation script failures.
real_world_scenario: A deployment script uses the wrong variable value because a global variable overrides local configuration.

comparisons.summary: Local exists inside function while global exists throughout program.

definition: Functions are reusable blocks of code designed to perform specific tasks.
why_it_matters: Functions help build maintainable DevOps automation scripts.
real_world_scenario: A monitoring script uses separate functions for CPU check, memory check, and alerting.

comparisons.summary: Function performs reusable logic while script executes workflow.

definition: args and kwargs allow functions to accept variable numbers of arguments.
why_it_matters: Automation scripts often need flexible inputs.
real_world_scenario: A deployment script accepts different server names and configuration options.

comparisons.summary: args handles values while kwargs handles key-value pairs.

definition: Modules and packages organize Python code into reusable components.
why_it_matters: Large DevOps automation projects require reusable code structure.
real_world_scenario: A company maintains common cloud automation utilities as reusable Python packages.

comparisons.summary: Module is one file while package contains multiple modules.

definition: A virtual environment creates an isolated Python environment with its own packages and dependencies.
why_it_matters: Different projects may require different library versions, and isolation prevents dependency conflicts.
real_world_scenario: A DevOps automation project requires requests version 2.x while another project requires a different version.

comparisons.summary: Global affects all projects while virtual environments isolate dependencies.

definition: pip is Python's package manager used to install, upgrade, and remove Python libraries.
why_it_matters: DevOps automation depends on external libraries for APIs, cloud, and Kubernetes.
real_world_scenario: A Jenkins pipeline fails because a required Python package is missing.

comparisons.summary: pip manages Python packages while apt manages OS packages.

definition: Python file handling allows scripts to create, read, modify, and manage files.
why_it_matters: DevOps scripts frequently process logs, configs, and deployment files.
real_world_scenario: A script reads application logs and extracts failed requests.

comparisons.summary: Read gets data while write stores data.

definition: OS automation uses Python libraries to interact with files, directories, and operating system functions.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers automate server operations using Python instead of manual commands.
real_world_scenario: A script automatically creates directories, moves deployment files, and cleans old data.

definition: Python subprocess module allows execution of Linux commands from Python scripts.
why_it_matters: DevOps automation often combines Python logic with Linux operations.
real_world_scenario: A Python deployment script runs kubectl, docker, or Linux commands automatically.

core_concepts.name: subprocess
core_concepts.definition: Python module for running external commands.

common_interview_questions: How execute shell command in Python?

definition: Exception handling allows Python programs to detect and handle runtime errors without crashing.
why_it_matters: Production automation scripts must handle failures gracefully.
real_world_scenario: A deployment script fails because an API is unavailable. Exception handling retries or reports the failure.

comparisons.summary: Errors are serious failures while exceptions can often be handled.

code_examples.title: Exception Example

definition: Python logging provides a structured way to record application events and errors.
why_it_matters: Production scripts require visibility instead of print statements.
real_world_scenario: A scheduled automation job fails overnight. Logs identify the exact failure.

core_concepts.name: Log Levels
core_concepts.definition: Severity levels like DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL.

comparisons.summary: print is temporary output while logging provides structured production tracking.

definition: Debugging is the process of identifying and fixing issues in Python programs.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers troubleshoot failed automation quickly.
real_world_scenario: A CI/CD pipeline fails because a Python deployment script throws an error.

comparisons.summary: Bug is a programming mistake while exception is runtime event.

definition: Regular expressions allow pattern matching and extraction of information from text.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers analyze logs and extract errors automatically.
real_world_scenario: A Python script scans application logs and finds failed requests.

definition: JSON handling allows Python programs to convert and process JSON data.
why_it_matters: Most DevOps tools communicate using JSON APIs.
real_world_scenario: A Python script reads cloud API responses and extracts resource details.

core_concepts.name: json.loads
core_concepts.definition: Convert JSON string to Python object.

definition: YAML is a human-readable configuration format commonly used in DevOps tools.
why_it_matters: Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure tools use YAML files.
real_world_scenario: A Python script reads Kubernetes YAML and validates deployment configuration.

definition: Environment variables store external configuration values that applications read at runtime.
why_it_matters: DevOps applications use environment variables for secrets, URLs, credentials, and deployment-specific configuration.
real_world_scenario: A Python deployment script reads database credentials and API keys from environment variables instead of hardcoding them.

comparisons.summary: Hardcoded values are unsafe while environment variables separate configuration from code.

definition: API automation uses Python libraries to communicate with services programmatically.
why_it_matters: Modern DevOps relies on APIs for cloud, CI/CD, monitoring, and infrastructure automation.
real_world_scenario: A Python script triggers a deployment API and validates application status.

core_concepts.name: requests library
core_concepts.usage: Send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests.

comparisons.summary: GET retrieves data while POST sends new data.

definition: Paramiko is a Python library used to perform SSH operations programmatically.
why_it_matters: Automation often requires executing commands on remote servers.
real_world_scenario: A Python script connects to multiple servers and checks application health.

core_concepts.name: SSH Client
core_concepts.definition: Object used to create remote connections.

common_interview_questions: How execute remote command using Python?

definition: Python is used in CI/CD pipelines to automate testing, deployment, validation, and reporting.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers integrate scripts into delivery workflows.
real_world_scenario: A Jenkins pipeline runs Python tests and deployment validation scripts.

definition: Cloud automation uses Python SDKs to create and manage cloud resources.
why_it_matters: Infrastructure automation reduces manual cloud operations.
real_world_scenario: A Python script creates cloud instances and manages storage automatically.

core_concepts.name: SDK
core_concepts.definition: Software Development Kit for cloud services.

definition: Kubernetes Python client allows automation and management of Kubernetes resources using Python.
why_it_matters: DevOps teams automate cluster operations and monitoring.
real_world_scenario: A Python script checks pod status and restarts unhealthy workloads.

architecture_flow.diagram: Python → K8s Client → API Server → Cluster

core_concepts.name: Kubernetes API
core_concepts.definition: Interface to interact with cluster resources.

definition: Python monitoring scripts collect system metrics like CPU, memory, disk, and process usage.
why_it_matters: DevOps engineers automate health checks and alerting.
real_world_scenario: A Python script checks server resources every minute and sends alerts when CPU crosses limits.

core_concepts.name: Health Check
core_concepts.definition: Validation that system is running correctly.

comparisons.summary: Manual checks require humans while scripts continuously monitor.

resolution_prevention.anti_pattern: Waiting for users to report issues.

definition: pytest is a Python testing framework used to validate application and automation scripts.
why_it_matters: DevOps pipelines require automated testing before deployment.
real_world_scenario: A CI pipeline runs Python tests before releasing an application.

core_concepts.name: Unit Test
core_concepts.definition: Tests a small part of code.

comparisons.summary: Automation provides repeatable validation.

definition: Threading and multiprocessing allow Python programs to perform multiple tasks concurrently.
why_it_matters: Automation tasks may need faster execution.
real_world_scenario: A script checks hundreds of servers simultaneously.

core_concepts.name: Thread
core_concepts.definition: Lightweight execution unit inside a process.

comparisons.summary: Threads share memory while processes have separate memory.

definition: Generators create values lazily instead of storing all results in memory.
why_it_matters: Large DevOps data processing requires memory efficiency.
real_world_scenario: A script processes millions of log lines without loading everything into memory.

definition: Decorators modify or extend function behavior without changing original code.
why_it_matters: Used for logging, authentication, and reusable behavior.
real_world_scenario: A decorator logs execution time of deployment functions.

definition: Production-ready Python scripts are designed with reliability, logging, error handling, and maintainability.
why_it_matters: DevOps scripts directly affect production systems.
real_world_scenario: A deployment automation script supports retries, rollback, and detailed logging.

comparisons.summary: Production scripts include validation, monitoring, and recovery.

common_interview_questions: How make Python script production ready?
